item.title: Explicit Error Term in the Chebotarev Density Theorem for Function Fields
item.description: We prove an explicit error term in the Chebotarev Density Theorem for finite generically Galois \'etale morphisms of affine varieties over finite fields, under a mild condition on their size. The error term generalises the known results for curves, and depends only on invariants of the varieties. We present several applications to the explicit error term. We apply it to existence problems, and to the Bateman-Horn conjecture over finite fields.

item.title: The Tate Conjecture in Positive Characteristic
item.description: Let $\mathcal{Z}(n)$ be Bloch's cycle complex and $\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ be the complex that compute continuous \'etale cohomology. Kahn observed that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to the map $\mathcal{Z}(n)\otimes\mathbb{Z}(0)^c\to\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ being isomorphism. Later, Kahn found that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to $\Omega_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{\'et}}(k)$, where $\Omega_\ell$ is the right adjoint of the $\ell$-adic realisation functor. In this note, using the Dwyer-Greenlees equivalence between $\ell$-completed objects and $\ell$-torsion objects, we prove that $\Omega_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{\'et}}(k)$, and consequently, based on Kahn's early work, the Tate conjecture at positive characteristics.

item.title: Reduction types of curves in tame extensions
item.description: Let $C/K$ be a curve of genus $g\geq 1$ over a discretely valued field $K$ with algebraically closed residue field. In this paper, we study the behaviour of the reduction type of $C$ under finite tame extensions. If $L/K$ is a tame extension of degree $n$, we give sufficient conditions on the reduction type $R$ of $C$ so that the reduction type of the base change $C_L$ is uniquely determined by $R$ and $n$. In particular, if $C$ has abelian and toric ranks zero, then $R$ satisfies these conditions. We also give an algorithm to compute the possibilities for the reduction type of $C_L$ given only $R$ and $n$. The main method involves studying harmonic covers of graphs with a cyclic action. As a result, we obtain a characterisation of tame curves with potentially good reduction in terms of their reduction type, and a new proof of a result by Liu-Lorenzini-Raynaud regarding the non-realisability of certain reduction types.

item.title: Recurrence formulas for Taylor expansions at CM points on genus-one and genus-two Shimura curves
item.description: We establish a general differential equation relating the expansion of a weight-two eigenform $f$ on a Shimura curve to the Schwarzian derivative $\mathcal{R}$ associated with $f$. When the quotient $X/W$ has genus zero, we introduce a Hauptmodul $u$ and obtain a coupled system of differential equations involving $f$, $\mathcal{R}$, and $u$. Geometric information, including local constraints on the poles of $\mathcal{R}$, together with the initial coefficients of the expansion of $f$, determine all the parameters in the system. We apply this method to all twelve weight-two eigenforms on Shimura curves $X_0^N(1)$ of genus one or two, obtaining explicit recurrence formulas for their Taylor expansions at selected CM points, conditional on the numerically recognized initial coefficients. As an application, we use the coefficients obtained from the recurrence to compute the Shimura uniformization $\Phi: \operatorname{Jac}(X)\to E$ to high precision and identify a large family of CM points on the associated elliptic curves $E$.

item.title: Improved bounds for the binary Chowla conjecture
item.description: For the M\"obius function $\mu$ and every fixed $0 < \epsilon < 1$, we prove \[ \sum_{n \le x} \mu(n) \mu(n + 1) \ll_{\epsilon} \frac{x}{(\log x)^{1 - \epsilon}}. \] This improves on OpenAI's recent bound of $x/(\log x)^c$, where $c > 0$ is a tiny absolute constant. The proof echoes the graph expansion framework of Helfgott, Radziwill, and Pilatte on the logarithmic Chowla conjecture, earlier Fourier analytic methods of Matom\"aki, Radziwill, and Tao on the Chowla conjecture on average, as well as work of Ter\"av\"ainen and the author for M\"obius on shifted primes. This also yields an improved result, \[ \sum_{p \le x} \mu(p + 2) \ll_{\epsilon} \frac{\pi(x)}{(\log x)^{1/2 - \epsilon}}. \] Specifically, we refine the determinant approach from the Poisson-Dirichlet law for prime predecessors. We replace the averaged prime weights of L\"u-Wang-Wu with an exact partition of prime intervals. Once sieving out exceptional integers, this enables uniform cancellation with arbitrary log power savings.

item.title: Uniform counting of quadratic fields with local conditions
item.description: We sharpen the uniform counting estimates of Bhargava, Thorne, and the author for quadratic fields with prescribed local conditions. Combining the Burgess and P\'olya--Vinogradov bounds, we improve the dependence of the error term on the primes supporting the local conditions and make explicit the factors previously absorbed into an arbitrary $\epsilon$-power of their product. The resulting estimate has an absolute implied constant.

item.title: Stepanov's method and uniform sumset estimates in arbitrary finite fields
item.description: Let $A<\mathbb F_q^\times$ be a proper multiplicative subgroup that generates $\mathbb F_q$ over its prime field. We prove that \[ |A+A|\ge \tfrac18|A|^{3/2} \] whenever $|A|<q^{2/3}$, uniformly in the characteristic and extension degree, without quantitative restrictions on intersections with proper subfields. Moreover, in contrast with what is expected in prime fields, we show that no uniform bound with exponent larger than $5/3$ holds in $\mathbb F_q$ even for $|A| \approx q^{1/2}$. The proof's key idea is to run the prime-field Stepanov method in reverse, constructing an auxiliary polynomial whose specialization vanishes identically instead of requiring it to be nonzero.

item.title: A two-sided continued-fraction criterion for the Erd\H{o}s-Moser equation and Erd\H{o}s's 1949 problem
item.description: We give a two-sided continued-fraction criterion for the Erd\H{o}s--Moser equation $1^k+2^k+\dots+(m-1)^k=m^k$. Writing $m=k/\log 2+3/2+\gamma_m/m$, Gallot, Moree and Zudilin showed that a solution yields a convergent of $\log 2/(2N)$, for a known divisor $N$ of $k$, followed by a large partial quotient. We show that an explicit two-sided estimate for $\gamma_m$, from our earlier centre-of-mass work, restricts this partial quotient, for each value of $\gcd(k/N,2m-3)$, to two consecutive values, or to three in the exceptional case that an integer lies in an explicit interval of relative length $O(1/m)$. This excludes the first index left open by their computation and, without extending their continued-fraction computation, raises the lower bound for a nontrivial solution from $m>2.71\cdot 10^{1667658416}$ to $m>6.26\cdot 10^{1667658425}$. The same criterion gives an effective form of the asymptotic results of Best and te Riele on Erd\H{o}s's 1949 problem on the largest term of $1^n+\dots+(m-1)^n$. We determine all 50 pairs $(m,n)$ with $m<10^{399}$ for which $(m-2)^n<(m-1)^n/2$ and $1^n+\dots+(m-1)^n>m^n$; in particular, the smallest e

item.title: Foata and Spot Commutation for Parking Functions
item.description: For a parking function $\alpha$, let $\mathrm{spot}(\alpha)$ be the permutation whose $i$th entry is the space occupied by car $i$ and let $\mathrm{foata}(w)$ be Foata's second fundamental transformation on words. Conjecture 6.3 of Celano et al. asserts that $\mathrm{foata}(\mathrm{spot}(\alpha)) = \mathrm{spot}(\mathrm{foata}(\alpha))$ for every unit interval parking function $\alpha$. This paper proves the identity for a larger class: parking functions where each prime component (borrowing Gessel's definition) of $\alpha$ is nondecreasing. Since every unit interval parking function is composed of nondecreasing prime parking functions, the conjecture follows. A key step is showing that $\mathrm{foata}$ preserves the set of parking functions $\alpha$ with $\mathrm{spot}(\alpha) = \mathrm{std}(\alpha)$, where $\mathrm{std}$ denotes standardization. In particular, this proves that inversion count and major index are equidistributed over this larger class.

item.title: Forsyth--Glaisher-Type Series for $1/\pi$ Involving Catalan Numbers and Harmonic Numbers
item.description: We develop an elementary method for constructing and evaluating families of Forsyth--Glaisher-type series for $1/\pi$. The approach is based on Newton's generalized binomial theorem, identities for generalized binomial coefficients, and Euler's beta integral, together with properties of the gamma and digamma functions. We establish several parameterized identities involving squares of central binomial coefficients and products of odd integers, from which we derive explicit evaluations in terms of $1/\pi$. By means of transformations connecting generalized binomial coefficients with Catalan numbers, we obtain further families of series involving squares of Catalan numbers. We also derive identities for series involving harmonic and odd harmonic numbers by differentiating suitable parameter-dependent formulas. These results yield evaluations containing both $1/\pi$ and logarithmic terms, particularly $\ln 2$. Our results provide a unified framework for generating and evaluating related binomial and Catalan-type series and reveal connections among central binomial coefficients, Catalan numbers, and harmonic numbers.

item.title: Short Paper No. 2: Relations between integer sequences A003622 $\&$ A035336 and two criteria in respect of maximum degrees within the family of finite linear Jaco graphs
item.description: This paper establishes two relationships between integer sequences and the maximum degrees of finite linear Jaco graphs $J_n(x)$. First, it characterizes the positive maximum degrees that occur exactly once within the family, showing that they are generated by the integer sequence A003622. Second, it determines the orders of the corresponding graphs and establishes their relationship with the integer sequence A035336. These results resolve conjectures previously stated in [5]. The proofs were developed with the assistance of AI-based mathematical reasoning technology and subsequently reviewed by the authors.

item.title: The Rotation Strategy Wins Penney's game for Permutations
item.description: In Penney's game for permutations, two players choose distinct patterns of the same length $k$, and independent random variables with a common continuous distribution are observed until the relative order of $k$ consecutive observations matches one of the patterns; the player who chose that pattern wins. Elizalde and Lin conjectured that the second player wins with probability greater than one half by answering the pattern $a_1a_2\cdots a_k$ with its rotation $a_ka_1\cdots a_{k-1}$. We prove that this conjecture holds for every $k\ge3$. We also show that for $k\ge8$ the rotation wins with probability at least $1/2+0.0053/(k+1)$. The proof writes the advantage of the second player in terms of clusters, which are chains of overlapping marked occurrences of the two patterns weighted by $\pm1$. We show that, for each ordering of the observations, the weights of its clusters sum to $-1$, $0$, or $1$. This gives an explicit bound on the contribution of arbitrarily long clusters, which proves the result analytically for $k\ge8$, and exact rational computations prove it for $3\le k\le7$.

item.title: Combinatorial Zeta Functions of Type $\widetilde A_2$
item.description: We develop a combinatorial zeta theory for finite colored triangular complexes $X$ whose vertex links satisfy a local hexagon condition. Their edge and chamber zeta functions $Z_1(X,u)$ and $Z_2(X,u)$ are Euler products over primitive closed geodesics. The M\"obius functions of the augmented local incidence posets define a vertex polynomial $M(X,u)$. We prove the identity $\frac{Z_1(X,u)}{Z_2(X,-u)} = (1-u^3)^{\chi(X)}M(X,u)^{-1}$, where $\chi(X)$ is the Euler characteristic of $X$. The proof reconstructs the cohomological operator framework for finite $\mathrm{PGL}_3$ quotients from the local link data: the degree operators recover the three determinant factors and together form a cochain map homotopic to multiplication by $1-u^3$. Sylvester's identity gives the resulting alternating determinant relation directly. All constructions use only the finite incidence structure of $X$; no ambient group, field, or building is required.

item.title: Quadratic periods and preperiods in subtraction games with one varying move
item.description: We give two infinite families of counterexamples to Zhang's conjectures on the period and preperiod of the Sprague-Grundy sequence when a single move c is adjoined to a fixed subtraction set S. For S = {4,5,10} and c = 15t+13 with t >= 2, the least period is c+19 and the least preperiod is (c^2+21c+8)/15. For S = {3,7,10} and c = 90t+9 with t >= 1, the least period is (c^2+26c+615)/30 and the least preperiod is 19 less than the period. The latter quadratic period also occurs in the outcome sequence, which is periodic from its first term. The proofs construct the sequences from fixed words and reduce the mex recurrence to a finite table of local identities.

item.title: Face-neighbourly polyhedra with eight or nine faces and genus at most three
item.description: A polyhedral surface is face-neighbourly if every pair of faces shares an edge. We classify the combinatorial types of closed orientable face-neighbourly polyhedral surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with eight or nine faces and genus at most three, assuming trivalent vertices, simple planar polygonal faces and distinct supporting planes for adjacent faces. Several common edges between a pair of faces are allowed. The enumeration gives 42,124 candidate maps with eight faces and 203 with nine. SAT certificates exclude all but two maps, both of genus three with eight nonagonal faces. They are realised by Mizhaev's V2 and by the R\"ost--V\'igh polyhedron. With the face-neighbourliness condition removed, the class of genus-three surfaces with eight nonagonal faces has one additional realisable type, Mizhaev's V1.

item.title: Externally supported independence in split and proper interval graphs
item.description: An independent set $B$ in a graph $G=(V,E)$ satisfying the additional condition that the vertices in $N(B)$ are dominated by vertices in $V(G) \setminus N[B]$ is called an externally supported independent set (ESI-set for short). The maximum cardinality of such a set in $G$ is called externally supported independence number of $G$. We study the externally supported independence number in split graphs and proper interval graphs, two graph classes with unbounded clique-width. For split graphs we investigate the structure and computational complexity of the ESI Set problem. We prove that the ESI Set problem remains NP-complete when restricted to split graphs, while also establishing simple upper and lower bounds for the externally supported independence number. These bounds are sharp for a wide range of split graphs. For split graphs, we further investigate the relationship between the externally supported independence number and the isolation number. In particular, we characterize when an optimal ESI-set yields an optimal isolating set, and conversely, when an optimal isolating set yields an optimal ESI-set. Finally, we consider proper

item.title: Raynaud and Gruson's flattening techniques in Berkovich geometry
item.description: Raynaud and Gruson introduced a flattening procedure for coherent sheaf in the schemes context that rely on sophisticated techniques of algebra and geometry. These methods were later used by Raynaud, Bosch and L\"utkebohmert in formal geometry, and more recently Ducros has developed analogous tools for Berkovich spaces. However, it should be noted that the expression "flattening by blowing up" is, in this context, a little abusive because the flattening process actually requires a succession of blow up and quasi-\'etale morphisms. The aim of this article is to develop a local flattening technique in Berkovich geometry, in the boundaryless case, which only involves blow up.

item.title: Spaces of ratios of schemes and \'etale cohomology
item.description: We introduce the arithmetic topologies on the spaces of ratios for log schemes and prove the basic properties of their cohomologies.

item.title: On the tensor product of semistable Hermitian adelic vector bundles over an adelic curve
item.description: We prove tensor semistability for Hermitian adelic vector bundles on proper adelic curves whose underlying fields are countable and of characteristic zero. The central estimate concerns the canonical integral Specht lattice of a rectangular partition with fixed height: its logarithmic covolume, divided by its rank and tensor degree, tends to zero. We prove this estimate from monic seminormal norms and an exact hypergeometric law weighted by the square of a Vandermonde product for tableau prefixes. Constant adelic Specht bundles and equivariant contractions then yield the slope inequality for every geometrically semistable subspace of a finite tensor product. The correction is the measure of the Archimedean places times a sublinear Specht term and vanishes in the limit as the auxiliary degree tends to infinity. An instability-filtration argument completes the reduction to arbitrary factors and identifies the tensor product Harder--Narasimhan filtration. The number field specialization gives the Bost tensor semistability conjecture in all ranks.

item.title: Stably irrational algebraically elliptic Fano threefolds
item.description: We establish algebraic ellipticity in the sense of Gromov of a general hypersurface of bidegree $(2,2)$ in $\mathbb P^2\times\mathbb P^2$. According to a theorem of B\"ohning and Graf von Bothmer, a very general such hypersurface is a stably irrational Fano threefold.

item.title: Arithmetic jet stacks
item.description: We construct a stack, which generalizes the notion of the arithmetic jet space functor constructed by Borger using the generalized Witt vector constructions. A priori we con- struct the jet space functor for prestacks, consequently showing that this functor preserves stacks. We then proceed to show the representability of the jet space functor applied to a representable morphism of stacks thereby showing that the jet space functor preserves algebraic and Deligne-Mumford Stacks. We also discuss the properties of morphisms preserved under the jet functor

item.title: Tannakian Brill-Noether theory of nodal curves
item.description: Using the Tannakian categories arising from convolutions of perverse sheaves on semi-abelian varieties, we can associate to any subvariety of a semi-abelian variety a reductive group together with a representation. We compute these groups and representations for Brill-Noether varieties of all curves whose generalized Jacobian is semi-abelian, in particular for nodal curves. We also obtain new results on the dimension and non-degeneracy of these Brill-Noether varieties.

item.title: Torrelli's Question for Isolated Hypersurface Singularities
item.description: Torrelli asked whether the class $[1/f]$ belongs to the intersection homology $\mathcal{D}$-module of a hypersurface if and only if $-1$ is a simple root of its local Bernstein-Sato polynomial. We prove this equivalence for isolated hypersurface germs with $2\le n\le 4$ variables, and we construct isolated counterexamples with $n$ variables for every $n\ge 5$. In fact a counterexample with $[1/f]\in\mathrm{IC}_D$ and $\mathrm{mult}_{s=-1}b_f(s)=r\ge 2$ always needs at least $r+3$ variables. The counterexamples modify a three-variable example of Saito and adjoin suitable pure powers in the new variables. We also show that a counterexample polynomial in $n$ variables needs at least $n+1$ monomials, and we record further cases in which the equivalence holds.

item.title: Finite abelian groups acting on rationally connected threefolds III: Classification
item.description: We complete the classification of finite abelian groups that admit a faithful action on a rationally connected threefold. For a finite abelian group $G$ with invariant factors $1<d_1\mid\cdots\mid d_s$, put $c(G)=\sum_i(1-1/d_i)$. We prove that for $1\le n\le3$ such a group admits a faithful action on a rationally connected variety of dimension $n$ if and only if $c(G)\le n$. We also show that finite abelian subgroups of the Cremona group of rank three are, up to isomorphism, precisely the products of finite abelian subgroups of the Cremona groups of ranks one and two. Four further groups can act faithfully on rationally connected threefolds. For each of these groups, the faithful action is unique up to birational conjugacy and automorphism of the acting group.

item.title: Geometric foundations of mesoscopic nucleation theory: commutativity of kinetic and probabilistic reduction for the Dean-Kawasaki equation
item.description: The reduction of a stochastic field equation to a few degrees of freedom is a central problem in many areas of physics, applied mathematics and engineering. In this work we present two routes for the dimensional reduction of conservative stochastic partial differential equations of Dean-Kawasaki type. To our knowledge, such reductions have always been carried out at the level of the trajectories, i.e. on Dean's equation, and never at the level of the probability distribution, i.e. on Kawasaki's equation. The first route starts from the parametrisation of the density introduced by Lutsko [J. F. Lutsko, J. Chem. Phys. 136, 034509 (2012)], who imposed it on the field equation and obtained stochastic equations for the order parameters by integrating against a suitable weight. The second route, which reduces Kawasaki's equation, is new. This route averages the functional forward Kolmogorov equation over the fast transverse degrees of freedom, using Fermi tubular coordinates around the manifold. Since the equations of Dean and Kawasaki are formally equivalent, one would expect both reductions to be equivalent as well. We show that this is n

item.title: Epidemic random model under vaccination regime and non-permanent immunity driven by time-changed Levy noise
item.description: A random version of the Susceptible-Infected-Recovered-Vaccinated (SIRV) epidemic model with non-permanent immunity and a population of non-constant size is studied. The compartments satisfy a system of differential equations in which the contact rate is a random coefficient, and the contact rate itself is driven by a stochastic differential equation with time-changed Levy noise. This noise is constructed from a conditional Brownian motion and a doubly stochastic Poisson random field, both governed by a stochastic clock. When the clock is independent of the Brownian and Poisson components, the two parts of the noise are a time-changed Brownian motion and a time-changed Poisson random measure. The equation for the contact rate decouples from the compartment equations and enters them as a random parameter, which allows the compartments to be treated pathwise. The existence, uniqueness, and positivity of the global solution are proven, and the basic reproduction number of the model is shown to be random. Furthermore, sufficient conditions for extinction and persistence in mean of the disease are derived. The conditions are expressed in t

item.title: Fermat costs and path-dependent first-passage percolation
item.description: We introduce a path-dependent and space-inhomogeneous first-passage percolation (FPP) model in the continuum. Inspired by Euclidean FPP, it is defined through a sample of points drawn from a common density function on a Riemannian manifold. In Euclidean FPP, the cost of each step in a discrete path is given by its length raised to the power $\alpha>1$. In our model, the power $\alpha$ increases as the path progresses, governed by a control mechanism. Consequently, the resulting percolation cost is not a distance. However, we prove a shape theorem showing that, as the number of points goes to infinity, the percolation costs converge to deterministic space-time integrals along curves in the manifold. This limit defines a quasi-distance with the property that traversing a curve from a high-density region towards a low-density one is generally cheaper than in the reverse direction; thus highlighting its potential use in machine learning applications.

item.title: Tight Lipschitz Hardness for Solving Random Polynomial Equations
item.description: We consider the problem of solving $n$ polynomial equations in $d$ real variables: $F_1({\boldsymbol x})=0, \ldots, F_n({\boldsymbol x})=0$, with unknowns ${\boldsymbol x}=(x_1, \ldots, x_d)$ satisfying the normalization constraint $\|{\boldsymbol x}\|=1$, when the polynomials are i.i.d. realization of a rotationally invariant Gaussian process. In previous work (Montanari, Subag, 2023), we developed an iterative algorithm that attempts to minimize the energy function $H({\boldsymbol x})=\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})\|^2/2$ (with ${\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})=(F_i({\boldsymbol x}):i\le n)$), using first and second order information (gradient and Hessian of $H$) at a sequence of query points ${\boldsymbol x}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol x}_k$. Here, we prove a lower bound on the minimum energy achieved by any algorithm that is Lipschitz continuous in the coefficients of the polynomials $F_i$. We prove that the lower bound matches the the energy achieved by the algorithm in (Montanari, Subag, 2023), hence characterizing the degree of accuracy to which the system of equations ${\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})={\boldsymbol 0}$ can be s

item.title: Limit distributions and bootstrap for smooth adapted Wasserstein distances
item.description: In this paper, we provide limit theorems for the Gaussian-smoothed adapted Wasserstein distances. Let $\widehat{\mu}_n$ be the empirical measure of independent paths with law $\mu$ on $(\mathbb{R}^d)^T$. Let $P = \mu * \gamma_\sigma$ and $P_n = \widehat{\mu}_n * \gamma_\sigma$, where $\gamma_\sigma = N(0,\sigma^2 I_{dT})$ is a Gaussian measure with mean zero and covariance matrix $\sigma^2 I_{dT}$. We first assume that $\mu$ is compactly supported. For every $1 < p < \infty$ and fixed $d, T$, and $\sigma > 0$, we show that $\sqrt{n}\,\mathrm{AW}_p(P_n,P) \Rightarrow Q_{P,p}(G)^{1/p}$, where $G$ is the Gaussian limit of the density fluctuation and $Q_{P,p}$ is the minimum adapted $p$-energy for the linearized continuity equation. We prove full-path bootstrap consistency and the convergence of the first and $p$-th moments. The limit and the bootstrap hold for noncompact laws as well, for all $1 < p < \infty$ under appropriate tail and structural conditions. For two-sided bounded density perturbations of strongly log-concave laws, the bandwidth is not restricted for $1 < p \le 2$. For $p > 2$, we give sufficient tail conditions and provi

item.title: The shortest figure-eight geodesics on random hyperbolic surfaces
item.description: We consider primitive unoriented figure-eight geodesics on a closed hyperbolic surface of genus $g$ sampled from Weil--Petersson measure. The shortest of these geodesics realizes the non-simple systole. He, Shen, Wu and Xue proved that its length is tight after centering at $a_g=\log g-\log\log g$. We prove that, as $g\to\infty$, the point process of centered lengths converges to a Poisson process on $\mathbb R$ with intensity $e^s\,ds/(8\pi^2)$. Its first arrival gives a reflected Gumbel limit for the centered systole $M_g$. We also prove convergence of the marked process in which each figure-eight carries the three cuff lengths of its supporting pair of pants, normalized by their sum. In the limiting process, the third cuff accounts for half the perimeter. The two winding cuffs, ordered at random, divide the other half uniformly. These splits are independent across points and independent of the limiting lengths. Uniform exponential bounds on both tails of $M_g$ give convergence of all fixed polynomial moments. At the critical exponent $-1$, we obtain $\mathbb E_g e^{-M_g}\sim(\log g)/(16\pi^2)$.

item.title: Exact almost sure scale for non-negative stochastic recursions
item.description: We study exact almost sure scale for non-negative stochastic recursions whose conditional mean consists of a linear term and a signed adapted perturbation. The linear term determines a product normalization, but convergence after normalization does not ensure a strictly positive limit. Multiplying the state by the inverse of each deterministic contraction factor gives a contraction-adjusted state. On paths where this state tends to infinity, we prove that the logarithm of the normalized state differs from the cumulative relative perturbation by an almost surely convergent quantity. The assumptions control the effective step sizes, the quadratic positive relative perturbation, and the conditional quadratic variation of the relative martingale noise. If the positive perturbation is summable at the normalized scale, the normalized process converges to a finite non-negative limit; strict positivity is then equivalent to absolute summability of the relative perturbation. We also give criteria for divergence of the contraction-adjusted state, first-order comparisons, and counterexamples illustrating the role of the hypotheses. Harmonic step

item.title: Differentiability of the solution to an SPDE with respect to the model for the associated regularity structure
item.description: Given a stochastic partial differential equation that falls within the scope of the theory of regularity structures, we show that its solution is, in a suitable sense, a smooth function of the underlying model. This allows one to infer the regularity of the solution with respect to any perturbation of the noise from that of the model. As an application of our results, we provide an elementary proof of the Malliavin differentiability of solutions to a wide class of equations driven by Gaussian noises.

item.title: Adaptive Precision Incomplete Matrix Factorization
item.description: Incomplete factorizations are widely used to precondition Krylov subspace methods for solving large sparse linear systems. Recent work has explored computing approximate factorizations in low precision, but using only one uniformly low precision limits the achievable accuracy and can degrade the quality of the preconditioner. We propose adaptive precision incomplete factorization algorithms in which we store each entry of the factors in a precision chosen according to its magnitude and a target accuracy. We present a rounding error analysis showing that the adaptive precision threshold-based incomplete LU and incomplete Cholesky factorizations achieve a backward error of the order of the target accuracy. We also discuss how to incorporate pivoting and scaling and how to perform the triangular solves with the adaptive precision factors. Finally, we explain how the approach applies to memory-limited incomplete Cholesky factorizations by using the magnitude of the largest dropped entry as the target accuracy. Numerical experiments on a wide range of matrices from the SuiteSparse collection show that adaptive precision can substantially r

item.title: Sub-Riemannian flow matching
item.description: We study sub-Riemannian conditional flow matching (SRCFM) for generative transport with prescribed velocity constraints. Training uses paths between sampled source and target points whose velocities lie in the allowed horizontal directions at each state. A neural network takes time and the full state as input and predicts the coefficients of these directions, and the horizontal frame then determines the full velocity used for generation. We describe constructions based on Heisenberg geodesics and joint endpoint equations in free step-two Carnot groups. We propose a scalable piecewise algorithm that computes horizontal paths directly from their endpoints. A straight segment sets the horizontal coordinates, and a loop in those coordinates corrects the remaining vertical displacement. We verify the algorithm's endpoint accuracy to numerical precision in high-dimensional tests. Synthetic experiments illustrate approximate distribution transport along horizontal trajectories. On resized MNIST, we use the same construction to generate images from Gaussian inputs with fewer controls than pixels.

item.title: Data-driven discovery of sparse governing equations with parameterized operators
item.description: We study parameterized SINDy (pSINDy), an extension of the Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) framework for the discovery of parsimonious governing equations involving operators with unknown parameters such as fractional-order Caputo derivatives, fractional Laplacians, and parameterized kernel operators. The framework jointly identifies the unknown operator parameters and sparse library coefficients through a sparsity-promoting optimization problem. To solve this problem, we develop and analyze the parameterized sequentially thresholded least-squares (pSTLSQ) algorithm. In each iteration, it removes terms with small coefficients, updates the operator parameters by a fixed number of optimization steps that improve the fit of the remaining library terms, and refits their coefficients by least squares. Under suitable assumptions, we prove that pSTLSQ converges locally to a local minimizer and give sufficient conditions for identifying the terms present in the governing equation. Numerical experiments demonstrate recovery of governing equations from noisy synthetic data for fractional ODEs, fractional PDEs, and nonlocal d

item.title: A hybrid high-order discretization of a volume integral formulation for eddy currents on unstructured polyhedral meshes
item.description: Volume integral formulations are attractive for eddy-current simulation because they require a mesh only of the conducting region. However, their dense interaction matrices make it important to control the number of unknowns needed for a prescribed accuracy. We propose an arbitrary-order Hybrid High-Order discretization of a current-based volume integral formulation on general unstructured polyhedral meshes. The method combines high-order polynomial approximation with local mesh refinement around defects and material interfaces. For bounded positive spatially varying resistivity and magnetic permeability uniform throughout space, we establish well-posedness and a priori error estimates using a constructive right inverse of the discrete divergence. Numerical experiments demonstrate convergence for smooth solutions and compare mesh refinement with increasing the polynomial degree. Selected comparisons show that higher degree on coarser meshes can reduce the number of current unknowns coupled by the Green operator and the associated storage for a prescribed accuracy. Finally, a three-dimensional eddy-current testing benchmark assesses th

item.title: Deterministic regularisation of the nonsymmetric eigenproblem
item.description: We give a deterministic algorithm for pseudospectral shattering in exact arithmetic. This resolves an important open problem in the complexity of the nonsymmetric eigenproblem. Given a complex contraction $A$ of order $n\ge2$ and $0<\delta<1/2$, we compute a perturbation $E$ with $\|E\|<\delta$ such that $A+E$ has simple spectrum. The ratio of its eigenbasis condition number to its minimum eigenvalue gap is at most $C(n/\delta)^{20/3}$. The algorithm also computes an exact eigensystem of $A+E$. It uses $O(n^3\log^d(n/\delta))$ real-field operations and comparisons, where $C$ and $d$ are absolute constants. We choose the rank-one perturbations using a lower bound on the circle mean of the logarithm of the discriminant modulus. A quadratic penalty controls how far the accumulated updates move the matrix. By using the same reference eigenbasis for several updates, we can estimate all the current projector norms while recovering only the directions needed for the next perturbation.

item.title: Finite-difference neural policy iteration for high-dimensional degenerate Hamilton--Jacobi equations
item.description: We develop a finite-difference neural policy iteration method for high-dimensional degenerate Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman and Isaacs equations. Artificial viscosity yields a monotone finite-difference operator, and neural networks approximate the linear equations of semi-discrete policy iteration using local stencil values. This avoids global tensor-grid storage. For measurable feedbacks, we bound the propagation of evaluation, terminal, gradient, and control optimization errors by a geometrically weighted sum. Discrete comparison, consistency, and vanishing viscosity relate the approximation to the original degenerate equation. On coupled manufactured problems with rank-deficient diffusion, the method achieves lower mean errors than direct physics-informed neural networks at every tested dimension from five to fifty under equal training time. At fifty dimensions and $900$ seconds, the mean relative $L^2$ error over three paired seeds is about $40\%$ lower. Two-dimensional refinement attains $0.297\%$ error against the original degenerate solution, with independent grid references separating approximation error from viscosity bias. In a

item.title: Numerical approximation of the Hilfer fractional derivative using orthogonal Quasi-Polynomials
item.description: A numerical approach based on a composite Gaussian quadrature for the Hilfer fractional derivative is presented. This approach employs quasi-polynomials that are orthogonal with respect to the weight function on the interval $(0,1)$. As special cases, the Riemann--Liouville and Caputo fractional derivatives are obtained. Error bounds for the approximation are derived. To confirm the convergence rates as well as the high efficiency of the new approach, numerical examples are provided.

item.title: Quantitative Convergence of the Spherical Brownian Motion collisional particle system for the Maxwellian Landau Equation
item.description: In this paper, we establish the quantitative convergence of the spherical Brownian motion (SBM) collisional particle system for the Maxwellian Landau equation via Wasserstein distances. When used as numerical method, it enjoys linear complexity $O(N)$ in particle number $N$, and conserves the momentum and energy almost surely. Moreover, only random grouping and sampling are needed for simulations without further numerical discretization. In the first part, we identify the large particle mean field limit of the system, and the Wasserstein convergence to the limit is justified through a coupling similar to the recent work for the Nanbu type Monte Carlo method \cite{BorghiPareschi2025}. The key difference is that the particles in our coupled shadow system are not i.i.d. due to the perfect matching. In the second part, the convergence of the mean field dynamics to the Landau solution is justified by the relative entropy with a bound $O(\tau^2)$, being $\tau$ the stepsize. This results in an $O(\tau)$ bound for the Wasserstein distance error. A crucial technical tool in the convergence in relative entropy is to provide suitable bounds on t

item.title: Dense ideals in forcing extensions of Nairian models
item.description: Complementing the work of Blue, Larson, and Sargsyan~\cite{NM,NM2}, we obtain forcing extensions of minimal Nairian models in which the Axiom of Choice and the Generalized Continuum Hypothesis hold. In these extensions, every uncountable regular cardinal $\kappa$ carries a precipitous, uniform, $\kappa$-dense ideal $\mathcal{I}_\kappa$. In fact, $\mathcal P(\kappa)/\mathcal{I}_\kappa$ is isomorphic to the regular open algebra of $\textrm{Col}(\omega,\kappa)$. This extends Woodin's theorem on the existence of $\omega_1$-dense ideals on $\omega_1$ in forcing extensions of models of $\Theta_{\rm reg}$ \cite[Section~2.3]{ASTWZ24}, where $\Theta_{\rm reg}$ denotes the theory $\textrm{ZF}+\textrm{AD}_{\mathbb R}+\text{``$\Theta$ is regular''}$. Moreover, our work places the consistency strength of the aforementioned theory on generic embeddings below a Woodin cardinal that is a limit of Woodin cardinals, and also complements the seminal work of Eskew and Hayut~\cite{EH24}.

item.title: A Note on the Topos-Inadmissibility of Free Heyting Algebras
item.description: Yiqi Xu and Linguan Ye have recently settled the long-standing open question about which Heyting algebras are topos-admissible, that is, occur as the truth values of some topos. They prove that free Heyting algebras with two or more generators are not topos admissible. Their proof has been simplified by Zoltan Kocsis and by Sam van Gool. Here I make some further simplifications, emphasising algebraic methods over Kripke semantics and in particular the use of Sierpi\'nski cones of Heyting algebras.

item.title: Taming Fitch's and Humberstone's Paradoxes
item.description: Fitch's Paradox says that if every true proposition is knowable, then every true proposition is known. Humberstone's Paradox states that if every true proposition is known by at least one of a set of finitely many agents, then some agent in that set knows every true proposition. Both paradoxes give rise to surprising and unacceptable consequences. In this paper, we diagnose a crucial tacit presupposition underlying these paradoxes, namely that the domain of propositions is closed under Boolean operations such as intersection and union, and offer a uniform resolution. We argue that the paradoxical inferences rely implicitly on this closure assumption. By adopting weak propositionally quantified modal logics that drop these closure conditions, we provide a semantically motivated account that blocks both paradoxes. The restriction on universal instantiation is not an ad hoc technical device, but reflects a conception of propositions as graspable objects of epistemic attitudes, on which the domain of propositions need not be closed under Boolean operations, since some Boolean combinations of graspable propositions may not themselves be gr

item.title: A logic of strong contingency
item.description: In this paper, inspired by the notions of contingency and strong possibility, we propose a notion which may be called 'strong contingency'. This notion can be seen as a mixture of contingency and strong possibility. We investigate the logic with strong contingency as a sole primitive modality, including its bisimulation notion, expressivity, frame definability, and axiomatizations. It turns out that this logic is expressively incomparable with the standard modal logic and the logic of contingency even over the class of S5-models, and less expressive than the logic of strong possibility and weak necessity over the class of S5-models. Besides, as the introduction of the inequality into the semantics makes the completeness proof much harder, instead of showing the completeness via a canonical model construction, we reduce the soundness and strong completeness of the involved proof systems to those of the existing proof systems in the literature.

item.title: $\Sigma^1_3$ Gandy-Harrington Forcing
item.description: Gandy-Harrington forcing is an important tool in descriptive set theory, first developed by Gandy and later used by Harrington to give a simple proof of Silver's dichotomy theorem. In this paper, we develop a new version of Gandy-Harrington forcing higher up in the projective hierarchy, under an appropriate local determinacy hypothesis. Using this new forcing, we prove a reverse mathematics result at the level of $\Delta^1_2$-Determinacy as well as new inner-model-theoretic basis theorem for $\Sigma^1_3$ sets.

item.title: The cardinal invariants of the $s$-dimensional Hausdorff null ideal are independent of $s$
item.description: For $0 < s < 1$, let $\mathcal{N}^s$ denote the ideal of sets of $s$-dimensional Hausdorff measure zero. We prove that $\operatorname{cov}(\mathcal{N}^s) = \operatorname{cov}(\mathcal{N}^t)$ and $\operatorname{non}(\mathcal{N}^s) = \operatorname{non}(\mathcal{N}^t)$ for all $0 < s, t < 1$. The proof uses Ren and Wang's solution of the Furstenberg set conjecture. This answers open questions of Shelah--Stepr\=ans and Elekes--Stepr\=ans.

item.title: On the uniformity of definably amenable radicals and dfg-fsg decompositions in $p$-adically closed fields
item.description: For definable families of groups over $p$-adically closed fields, we show that the definably amenable radicals and their dfg-fsg decompositions can be defined uniformly as the prime $p$ and the family parameters vary.

item.title: $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property
item.description: Let $(E, P)$, $(E', P')$ be elliptic curves over $\mathbb{C}$ with marked $p$-torsion points; a marked isogeny is an isogeny sending $P$ to $P'$. We show the marked isogeny relation is interpretable in $\mathbb{C}(t)$ and has strict infinite chains. It follows that $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property, which confirms a special case of the stable fields conjecture.

item.title: CausalNTP: A World-Model Recipe for Causal Next-Token Prediction under Noisy Training-data
item.description: This paper shows that transformer networks trained with next-token prediction (NTP) and gradient descent do not learn to make predictions using only causally-relevant tokens in the left context, irrespective of the causal ordering of tokens during training, and identifies the learning deficiencies responsible. We introduce a causal world-model setup, for which, we characterize the Bayes-optimal predictor under the causal view of the data. We then prove that, a function that distills its predictions to non-causal views of data, when realized under Occam's Razor, recovers the true causal predictor. Based on this analysis we propose CausalNTP, a practical training algorithm that approximates this theoretical recipe and trains transformers to depend only the causally relevant tokens in left-context. Empirically in the world-model setup, CausalNTP achieves out-of-distribution generalization that vanilla NTP cannot due to its theoretical limits, regardless of data and model scale. We show similar gains and behavior in the natural language question-answering setting as a proof-of-concept.

item.title: Persuasion from Within: Model-Based Insider Attacks in Multi-Agent LLM Debate and Consensus
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent systems for collective decision-making, such as multi-agent debate and consensus games, in which agents exchange messages and update their answers over multiple rounds and a resolution mechanism aggregates them into a final outcome. Most multi-agent LLM frameworks assume that every participant shares the system objective. In practice, however, a malicious agent can join as a legitimate member of the group and persuade the other agents toward a hidden adversarial goal. We formalize such attacks as a sequential decision-making problem in which the insider seeks to degrade the utility of the collective outcome. We propose a model-based insider attack that learns to persuade a group of agents: the insider first learns a world model of the benign agents from offline trajectories and then uses it both to train a persuasion policy and to plan its messages. In two case studies involving a numerical consensus game and a multi-agent debate, the learned insider is the most effective and the stealthiest attack we evaluate, outperforming both prompt-based and trained LLM persuad
